```{r}
library(regcompR)
```

## The registry

`registry_table()` lists every family with its category, parameters,
status and the backends that support it.

```{r}
reg <- registry_table()
table(reg$category)
head(reg[, c("id", "category", "parameters", "status")])
capabilities("conway_maxwell_poisson")
```

Families are validated against reference implementations: densities
integrate or sum to one, distribution functions agree with numerical
integration, and random draws agree with the stated moments.

## Operators

Operators build new families from registered ones. The result is a family
like any other: it can be used in `distribution()` and `regcomp()`.

```{r}
zinb <- inflate("nb2")          # zero inflation
names(zinb$pars)
hnb <- hurdle("poisson")                        # hurdle at zero
tn <- truncate_dist("normal", lower = 0)        # truncation
mx <- mixture("normal", "normal")               # finite mixture
d <- distribution(mx, mu.1 = -2, sigma.1 = 1, mu.2 = 2, sigma.2 = 0.7, w2 = 0.4)
plot(d)
```

Further operators:

* `censor()`, `discretize()`, `round_dist()`, `transform_dist()`, `wrap()`, `weighted()`;
* `compound()` for mixtures over a parameter, such as the Poisson lognormal law;
* `cure()` for mixture cure survival models;
* `splice()` for body and tail composite laws;
* `convolve_dist()` for sums of independent variables;
* `copula_dist()` for bivariate copula models with any margins.

```{r}
emg <- convolve_dist("normal", "exponential")
prob(distribution(emg, mu.1 = 0, sigma.1 = 1, lambda.2 = 2), c(0, 1, 2))
sp <- splice("lognormal", "lomax")
plot(distribution(sp, mu.b = 0, sigma.b = 0.6, scale.t = 2, alpha.t = 2.5,
                  threshold = 2, w = 0.7), xlim = c(0, 8))
```

## Generators

Generators such as `kumaraswamy_g()`, `beta_g()`, `marshall_olkin()`,
`transmuted()` and `exponentiated()` produce the generalized families of
the distribution literature from any baseline.

```{r}
kw <- kumaraswamy_g("weibull")
names(kw$pars)
```

## Custom families

`custom_family()` registers a law from its log density; regcompR checks
that it is normalized.

```{r}
myexp <- custom_family("my_exponential", list(par_spec("rate", "positive", role = "rate")),
  lpdf = function(y, p) dexp(y, p$rate, log = TRUE),
  support = function(p) list(lower = 0, upper = Inf), check = list(rate = 2))
coef(regcomp(y ~ 1, family = myexp, data = data.frame(y = rexp(200, 2))))
```
